turns.prompt: Write a one-page announcement for the Harrowfield Field Station open house and save it as a document I can keep. Details: Saturday, April 11, 10am to 2pm, at the Lakeview Pavilion. Include a short schedule with three items and a line about who to contact (Dana Ruiz, events office).
Change the date to Saturday, April 18. Keep everything else exactly the same.

notes: Iterative drafting, the costliest engineerable usage pattern in production (docs/one-pagers/conversation-usage-patterns.md). A one-detail edit should revise the existing artifact once, not create a second copy. Efficiency is the point: update_artifact is full-replace today, so the edit turn's output tokens are a whole document; a patch-style edit would show here as a fall in outputTokens with the case still passing.

turns.prompt: Draft a short welcome note for new volunteers at the Harrowfield Field Station and save it as a document. Mention the orientation on Monday at 9am in Room 104.
Make the tone a little warmer, and add that lunch is provided at orientation.
One more change: add a line saying parking is free in Lot C.

notes: Three turns on one document, so the history carries two superseded full copies by the last turn: the drafting pattern's second cost, paid as input on every later call. Scored on the third turn; efficiency counts every turn.

turns.prompt: Write a one-page announcement for the Harrowfield Field Station open house and save it as a document I can keep. Details: Saturday, April 11, 10am to 2pm, at the Lakeview Pavilion.
Quick question about the draft: what time does the open house end? Reply with just the time.

notes: A question about a draft is answered from it, not by rewriting it. A rewrite here is the drafting pattern's waste with no edit to show for it.

turns.prompt: According to https://example.com, what is that domain meant to be used for? One sentence.

notes: The browsing pattern's cost is loop length: every extra fetch is another model call that re-reads the whole context. One named page needs one fetch.

turns.prompt: Fetch https://example.com and https://example.org. Do the two pages use the same main heading? Answer yes or no, then give the heading.

notes: Two named pages, two fetches. Both pages carry the heading "Example Domain" (as of 2026-11); if either changes, this case's expectation changes with it.

turns.prompt: Read https://example.com and summarize it in one sentence.
What was that page's main heading? Reply with just the heading.

notes: The page is already in the conversation, so a follow-up about what it said is answered from it. Re-fetching is a browsing loop's waste in miniature. An earlier version asked where the page linked; example.com no longer links anywhere (2026-11), and a question the first fetch's text cannot answer makes a re-fetch the right call. If a future change offloads small tool results out of history, the right fix is the offload rule, not this case.

turns.prompt: In the attached workbook, find the largest Equipment line on the Expenses sheet, then give me its approver code from the Approvals sheet. Reply with the line and the code.

notes: The spreadsheet pattern's cost is probe-and-retry loops (analyze_spreadsheet fails about 15% of calls in production). A two-sheet lookup fits in one analysis, plus at most a listing and one retry. EXP-0041 (2,400) is the largest Equipment line; its approver is AP-51. AP-77 belongs to EXP-0042, a Travel line.

turns.prompt: Two questions about the attached workbook's Expenses sheet: what is the total Amount of the Supplies lines, and how many Travel lines are there?

notes: Two questions about one sheet should share one analysis. Supplies: 310 + 95 = 405. Travel lines: EXP-0040, EXP-0042, EXP-0045.

turns.prompt: Using the attached workbook, what is the total Amount of the Travel lines on the Expenses sheet?
And what share of all expenses on that sheet is that, to the nearest percent?

notes: The follow-up reuses the first answer and needs at most one more analysis (the sheet total). Travel 4,815 of 10,940 is 44.0%.

turns.prompt: From the attached readings, what is the highest reading for each sensor? List the three.

notes: A nine-row CSV may reach the model as text or through the spreadsheet tools, depending on the deployment; either is fine, a loop is not. Maxima: S-1 40.4, S-2 46.3, S-3 41.7 (47.1 is S-3's digits swapped).
